Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — unexpected Q2 spike, options for top-up?

Hi Lukas,

Hope you had a good weekend. Quick note from the ops team: our usage spiked in Q2 after launching the new triage flow and we're likely to exceed our committed capacity by ~45% this quarter. Our renewal is scheduled for 2027-08-01 and procurement asked whether we can: 1) add a mid-contract top-up to cover the surge, and 2) align the top-up with the renewal so everything co-terms on 2027-08-01.

Can you share the available pathways (one-time top-up vs staggered top-ups, any uplift discounts for committing early, and how co-terming would affect billing/proration)? Procurement is on copy and wants high-level numbers to prepare a PO.

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of AI Ops, Cygnus Health
maya@cygnushealth.com

Attachments: Cygnus_MA_projections_Q3.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@cygnushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — unexpected Q2 spike, options for top-up?

Hi Maya — thanks for the heads-up and the projection file. Marking this as high priority. Quick summary of the options we'll put together for procurement:

- One-time top-up (immediate): add an incremental committed capacity for the remainder of the current term; billed pro-rata, no co-terming changes.
- Staged top-ups: two tranches (immediate + July) to smooth invoice impact; modest admin overhead.
- Early uplift + co-term: convert the top-up into a multi-quarter uplift that immediately increases committed capacity and harmonizes the contract to the renewal date; we'd offer a small volume discount for the larger commit.

I'll loop in pricing to lay out the numbers and proposed concession levels. Marissa — can you draft three concrete scenarios (dollars, effective unit price, invoice timing) and call out any downstream procurement/finance implications (PO timing, tax/invoice notes)?

Might be helpful if procurement confirms whether they can approve a PO ahead of the renewal or need the DocuSign in place first.

Best,
Lukas
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
lukas@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@cygnushealth.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — options & numbers attached

Hi Maya / Lukas,

Attached are three scenarios in the attached spreadsheet (Cygnus_MA_projections_Q3.xlsx) — I pulled the usage buckets from the file you sent and modeled effective unit prices:

Scenario A — Short top-up (fast):
- Add 50% committed capacity for remainder of term (billed pro-rata from effective date).
- No change to renewal date.
- Effective unit price: $0.0085/token (current list price = $0.010).
- Impact on Q2 invoice: ~+$28k.

Scenario B — Staged top-ups (smoothing):
- 30% immediate add, 20% add in July.
- Slightly higher admin and two invoices; effective unit price blended $0.0089/token.

Scenario C — Early uplift + co-term (recommended if you expect sustained growth):
- Convert the 45% spike into a new committed uplift that runs through the renewal and renews at co-term on 2027-08-01.
- Offer a 6% uplift discount (applied to the uplifted volume) for committing now.
- Blended effective price for uplift volume: $0.0079/token.
- Immediate invoice impact (pro-rata + first invoice of uplift): ~$21k.

Notes / procurement implications:
- Co-terming requires an amendment to be signed (DocuSign link below); finance needs the amendment copy + PO if they require POs to match contract dates.
- If procurement needs net-30 PO matching invoice dates, Scenario B or C can be structured to align billing windows.

Attachments: redwood-uplift-options-2up.pdf (two-up summary), Cygnus_MA_projections_Q3.xlsx (model)

Next steps suggested:
1) Procurement confirms PO timing and whether a single DocuSign amendment is acceptable.
2) If Scenario C preferred, we prepare an amendment and route for signature; if A/B preferred, we'll push a one-off order with clear invoice notes.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call today if that helps.

— Marissa
Senior Pricing Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks — this is very helpful. Procurement (cc) confirms they prefer a single amendment to co-term the uplift with our renewal on 2027-08-01. Their ask: can you provide an amendment draft and a high-level milestone/timeline so procurement and legal can queue review? Our preference is Scenario C if the 6% uplift discount holds; we need the amendment and a DocuSign path to present to finance by next Thursday.

Procurement note: we need the amendment to show adjusted committed units, effective date, and the new co-term date on the first page. PO will be raised within 3 business days of the amendment being returned to us.

— Maya
